summary_of_threads_started_this_week:
Mining for the testnet5 genesis block is scheduled in alignment with the upcoming mainnet retarget event at block 975,744, with supporting resources and documentation available for those contributing hashrate or wishing to participate in the network bootstrapping process ([mining guide](https://gist.github.com/ajtowns/ebb148819c6028387271e6f0dce5e1da), [solo-mining pool](https://lapis.erisian.com.au/chain.html)). Key changes to the genesis block format have been introduced, simplifying pooled mining and improving compatibility, while testnet5 connectivity is supported by public libbitcoin nodes and web explorers ([node status](https://libbitcoin.org/configuration/public.html), [web explorers](https://wormer.libbitcoin.net:58143), [project site](https://libbitcoin.org)).

Several proposals focus on quantum resistance and privacy. Zaenus et al. have introduced a draft BIP for a quantum-resistant address format, `bc1z`, leveraging ML-DSA-65 signatures for enhanced security against quantum adversaries, with design details, migration strategies, and a reference implementation provided ([btc-safe repository](https://github.com/Zaenus/btc-safe)). Concurrently, a post-quantum key establishment protocol for the P2P layer using ML-KEM-768 (FIPS 203) is under review, aiming to secure network traffic against future quantum threats while balancing bandwidth considerations ([FIPS 203](https://csrc.nist.gov/csrc/media/Events/2025/workshop-on-guidance-for-kems/documents/papers/kemeleon-paper.pdf)). Additionally, privacy-enhancing tools for Silent Payments, such as spscand by Zenul Abidin, have been released, offering robust transaction detection and monitoring capabilities without compromising user confidentiality ([spscand GitHub](https://github.com/ZenulAbidin/spscand)).

Security disclosures remain a priority, with recent critical vulnerabilities identified and addressed in Bitcoin Core, Core Lightning, and Eclair. Users are strongly advised to upgrade to patched versions to mitigate denial-of-service and mempool inconsistency risks ([Bitcoin Core advisories](https://bitcoincore.org/en/security-advisories/), [Core Lightning release](https://github.com/ElementsProject/lightning/releases/tag/v26.06.8), [Eclair patch details](https://github.com/ACINQ/eclair/blob/d769db070424ae0ab6c05975fd7c86dac8b3e1f4/docs/release-notes/eclair-v0.14.1.md)).

Further, advancements in cryptographic proofs and interoperability are demonstrated by the introduction of a STARK-based verifier for the Bitcoin UTXO set ([live demo](https://starknet-innovation.github.io/starked-bitcoin/), [source repository](https://github.com/starknet-innovation/starked-bitcoin)), and by a draft BIP standardizing payload exchanges between wallets and air-gapped signers, supporting modern protocols and multisignature workflows ([draft BIP](https://github.com/bitcoin/bips/pull/2353), [forum discussion](https://delvingbitcoin.org/t/qr-based-signing-flow-payloads-in-miniscript-context/2464)).

new_threads_this_week.title: Testnet 5 launch
new_threads_this_week.summary: - Mining for testnet5’s genesis block aligns with mainnet retargeting, featuring documentation and a 0% fee pool.  - Genesis block modifications include extranonce space, nVersion rolling, and pszTimestamp for textual commitment.  - Block height encoding differences can cause issues during blockchain initialization, affecting chain bootstrapping.

new_threads_this_week.title: BIP Draft Post-Quantum Address Format (bc1z) using ML-DSA-65
new_threads_this_week.summary: - A new Bitcoin address format, bc1z, uses ML-DSA-65 signatures for quantum-resistant security.  - The format commits to a SHA-256 hash of the public key, improving privacy and safety.  - Open-source tools and references are provided, with community feedback encouraged on design and deployment.

new_threads_this_week.title: Testnet5 Launch
new_threads_this_week.summary: - Two public libbitcoin nodes supporting bip54 are now accessible for peer connections on testnet5.  - Node status, configuration, and connectivity details are provided at the specified monitoring webpage.  - Blockchain explorers for testnet5 are available online, enabling convenient web-based data inspection.

new_threads_this_week.title: spscand and libspscan: a watch-only BIP352 scanner
new_threads_this_week.summary: - spscand detects and tracks silent payment outputs, spends, and reorganizations using privacy-preserving methods.  - It supports Bitcoin Core, BlindBit, and BIP158 sources, implementing strict isolation and constant-time cryptography.  - libspscan, the core C library, enables integration, efficiency, security, and passes comprehensive BIP352 and BIP158 tests.

new_threads_this_week.title: [BIP Draft] Signing message encoding
new_threads_this_week.summary: - A new draft BIP proposes standardizing interactions between wallets and external signers using multiple data transfer methods.  - The proposal incorporates advanced features like MuSig2 multisignature protocols and silent payment functionalities.  - Community feedback is encouraged to refine the proposal for broader wallet and signer compatibility.

new_threads_this_week.title: BIP Proposal: ML-KEM Key Establishment
new_threads_this_week.summary: - ML-KEM-768 is recommended for enhanced quantum security, balancing strength and bandwidth efficiency.  - Key exchange combines BIP-324 and ML-KEM shared secrets, ensuring secure connections throughout protocol operations.  - Feedback is requested on using ML-KEM-768 and whether to send encapsulation keys by default.

new_threads_this_week.title: Three Bitcoin Core security advisories
new_threads_this_week.summary: - Three critical security vulnerabilities were discovered and addressed in recent Bitcoin Core updates.  - The issues include mempool inconsistency, improper whitelist privileges, and a flawed witness malleation check.  - Users and node operators should promptly upgrade to patched versions to maintain network security.

new_threads_this_week.title: Disclosure: Memory-exhaustion DoS in Eclair 0.14.0
new_threads_this_week.summary: - Eclair 0.14.0’s improper batch size validation allowed attackers to exhaust node memory remotely.  - Attackers could buffer unlimited messages without requiring open channels, causing denial-of-service conditions.  - Version 0.14.1 fixed this vulnerability by enforcing correct batch size and robust input validation.

new_threads_this_week.title: BIP Draft Post-Quantum Address Format (bc1z) using ML-DSA-65
new_threads_this_week.summary: - A new Bitcoin address format using ML-DSA-65 aims to provide quantum-resistant security for funds.  - The design employs SHA-256 commitments, maintains soft fork compatibility, and offers an open-source implementation.  - Feedback is requested on the format details, migration strategies, and whether early adoption is worthwhile.

new_threads_this_week.title: A STARK proof of Bitcoin's UTXO set at block 972,500, with circuits proven in Lean
new_threads_this_week.summary: - A new project presents a STARK-based cryptographic proof for Bitcoin’s header chain and UTXO set.  - The proof is compact, efficiently verifiable, includes raw block replay, but omits script validation and signatures.  - Supporting tools and documentation enable independent verification and alignment with Bitcoin Core’s rules and outputs.

new_threads_this_week.title: Disclosure: DoS vulnerability fixed in Core Lightning v26.06.8
new_threads_this_week.summary: - A denial-of-service vulnerability in Core Lightning allowed attackers to exploit duplicate funding outpoints.  - This flaw caused assertion failures and persistent crashes when affected nodes attempted to reconnect or close channels.  - Users should upgrade to the latest release to mitigate these risks and protect their nodes.

new_threads_this_week.title: Silent Payments for Electrum
new_threads_this_week.summary: - A new open-source tool, spscand, now complements the Silent Payments sending plugin for Electrum.  - spscand scans and monitors Silent Payments, prioritizing privacy and offering flexible integration options.  - The project emphasizes security, supports Tor, and encourages user feedback for further improvement.

active_posts_this_week.title: [BIP Proposal] Stale Tip Relay
active_posts_this_week.summary: - Three operational modes for stale tip relay are configurable, with defaults and future adjustments under discussion.  - Relaying stale blocks enhances transparency, reveals attacks, and provides robust evidence against malicious activity.  - Restricting honest relay may empower attackers, while transparency and mainnet proof improve overall network security.

active_posts_this_week.title: [BIP Proposal] Transport Feature Negotiation
active_posts_this_week.summary:
- A draft Bitcoin Improvement Proposal is available for review, including decisions on unresolved questions.
- Community feedback is encouraged to refine and strengthen the proposal for broader benefits.
- Interested individuals are invited to review the draft and comment through the linked GitHub platform.

active_posts_this_week.title: Gossip Observer: New project to monitor the Lightning P2P network
active_posts_this_week.summary: - Set reconciliation allows attackers to equivocate messages, causing hidden network partitions and inconsistent views.  - Attackers exploit this to fingerprint senders, divert traffic, and manipulate routing fees for personal gain.  - Cryptographic commitments and tree-based structures let nodes efficiently detect, localize, and prove message discrepancies.

active_posts_this_week.title: Towards A K-of-N Lightning Network Node
active_posts_this_week.summary: - The signer group design leverages VPSS1 over replicated PRF keys for managing keys and secrets.  - Operational rules support secure participation, fault-tolerant revocation, and flexible closing or splicing processes.  - Open questions involve optimal parameters for signer agreement, inviting further expert feedback on security requirements.

active_posts_this_week.title: [BIP Draft] Co-signer Spending Policies
active_posts_this_week.summary: - Current Bitcoin co-signing solutions lack standardization, leading to vendor lock-in and limited auditability.  - The proposed open format standardizes co-signer spending policies without requiring Bitcoin protocol changes.  - Adoption needs critical feedback, technical discussion, and real-world interoperability between independent implementations.

active_posts_this_week.title: Should wallets default to Taproot or SegWit receive addresses while some services still reject bc1p?
active_posts_this_week.summary: - The whentaproot.org website tracks Taproot support across wallets and requires periodic accuracy updates.  - Binance now demonstrates Taproot capability with valid withdrawal transactions, indicating increased adoption among major exchanges.  - Regularly updating and verifying such resources ensures users receive reliable information about Taproot integration.

active_posts_this_week.title: Decentralized Coinbase Payout Protocols (DCPP): A Framework for Discussion
active_posts_this_week.summary: - Standardized terms like PSG and RLA improved clarity and precision in decentralized mining pool discussions.  - P2Pool struggled with small miner payouts due to share difficulty thresholds and the dust rule.  - Incentive misalignments and payout system griefing present ongoing challenges for decentralized, trustless protocol design.

active_posts_this_week.title: We made the bitcoin-dev mailing list readable: 15 years, 24,699 messages
active_posts_this_week.summary: - The Bitcoin BIP archive now includes a section detailing BIP integration and version history in Core.  - Documentation covers all 74 BIPs and provides detailed pages for 137 Bitcoin Core releases since 0.1.5.  - Archive refreshes twice daily, with improved user profiles and complete listings accessible online.
